title: Maintenance, Assets, Compliance & Integrations
brief: Final milestone for the Business Management track. Covers the full maintenance lifecycle (preventive maintenance schedules, work orders, parts/labor tracking), equipment asset registry with depreciation, calibration management frontend wired to the existing CalibrationEngine, OSHA safety compliance logs, ISO/AS9100 internal audit management with 8D CAPA workflow, full 8D enhancement to QualityManagementEngine, and three integration connectors (E2 Shop System bidirectional sync, QuickBooks deep invoice/payment sync, email/SMS/in-app notifications wired to NotificationEngine). All engines either exist or extend existing ones — no greenfield physics.

phases.title: Maintenance & Asset Management
phases.description: Create PreventiveMaintenanceEngine from scratch and wire it to a calendar-based frontend page. Create EquipmentAssetEngine with depreciation math. Add the MaintenanceWorkOrderPage for create/assign/complete task flow. Wire CalibrationEngine (already 334 lines) to a new CalibrationPage with gage R&R display, certificate upload, and out-of-cal lockout.

units.title: Create PreventiveMaintenanceEngine + PreventiveMaintenancePage

steps.instruction: Read src/engines/CalibrationEngine.ts (first 60 lines) to understand the singleton export pattern, PersistenceBridge wiring style, and dispatcher action naming convention used in this codebase before writing any new engine code
Read src/tools/dispatchers/businessDispatcher.ts (first 80 lines) to confirm the z.enum action list structure and lazy-import pattern for engines

Create src/engines/PreventiveMaintenanceEngine.ts. Define interfaces: PMSchedule { id, machine_id, machine_name, task_name, trigger_type: 'calendar' | 'hours', interval_days: number | undefined, interval_hours: number | undefined, last_completed_at: string | undefined, last_completed_hours: number | undefined, parts_list: PMPart[], estimated_duration_min: number, instructions: string, created_at: string }, PMPart { part_name, part_number, quantity, unit_cost }, PMWorkOrder { id, schedule_id, machine_id, machine_name, task_name, parts_list: PMPart[], status: 'open' | 'in_progress' | 'complete' | 'cancelled', assigned_to: string | undefined, scheduled_date: string, completed_at: string | undefined, labor_hours: number | undefined, total_cost: number | undefined, notes: string | undefined, created_at: string }, MaintenanceDowntime { id, machine_id, type: 'scheduled' | 'unscheduled', started_at: string, ended_at: string | undefined, duration_min: number | undefined, work_order_id: string | undefined, cause: string | undefined }

Implement PreventiveMaintenanceEngine class with private Maps: pmSchedules: Map<string, PMSchedule>, pmWorkOrders: Map<string, PMWorkOrder>, maintenanceDowntime: Map<string, MaintenanceDowntime>. In constructor, call persistenceBridge.register() for all three Maps

Implement createSchedule(params): PMSchedule — validates that either interval_days (for calendar) or interval_hours (for hours) is present based on trigger_type, assigns a uuid-style id, stores in pmSchedules, calls persistenceBridge.persist('pm_schedules')

Implement listSchedules(filters?: { machine_id?: string; overdue_only?: boolean }): PMSchedule[] — returns schedules filtered by machine_id if provided. If overdue_only, filter using isScheduleDue() helper

Implement isScheduleDue(schedule: PMSchedule, currentHours?: number): boolean — for calendar type: returns true if Date.now() >= (last_completed_at date + interval_days * 86400000) OR if last_completed_at is undefined. For hours type: returns true if (currentHours - last_completed_hours) >= interval_hours OR if last_completed_hours is undefined

Implement generateWorkOrder(scheduleId: string, scheduledDate: string): PMWorkOrder — creates a PMWorkOrder from the schedule template, status = 'open', stores in pmWorkOrders, calls persistenceBridge.persist('pm_work_orders'). Throws if schedule not found. Throws if an open/in_progress work order already exists for the same schedule

Implement completeWorkOrder(workOrderId: string, params: { labor_hours: number; notes?: string; parts_used?: PMPart[] }): PMWorkOrder — sets status = 'complete', completed_at = ISO timestamp, labor_hours, notes. Calculates total_cost = sum of (parts_used quantity * unit_cost) + (labor_hours * 75) using a $75/hr default labor rate. Updates the parent schedule's last_completed_at. Calls persistenceBridge.persist('pm_work_orders') and persistenceBridge.persist('pm_schedules')

Implement getOverdueAlerts(currentMachineHours?: Map<string, number>): Array<{ schedule: PMSchedule; days_overdue: number; hours_overdue: number | undefined }> — iterates all schedules, calls isScheduleDue(), computes days_overdue as Math.floor((Date.now() - due_date_ms) / 86400000) for calendar type or hours_overdue for hours type

Implement recordDowntime(params: Omit<MaintenanceDowntime, 'id'>): MaintenanceDowntime — stores in maintenanceDowntime Map. If ended_at is provided, compute duration_min = (Date.parse(ended_at) - Date.parse(started_at)) / 60000. Calls persistenceBridge.persist('maintenance_downtime')

Add ENTITY_CONFIGS entries in src/db/BusinessStore.ts for pm_schedules (knownColumns: id, machine_id, machine_name, task_name, trigger_type, interval_days, interval_hours, last_completed_at, last_completed_hours, estimated_duration_min, instructions, created_at; jsonColumns: parts_list), pm_work_orders (knownColumns: id, schedule_id, machine_id, machine_name, task_name, status, assigned_to, scheduled_date, completed_at, labor_hours, total_cost, notes, created_at; jsonColumns: parts_list), maintenance_downtime (knownColumns: id, machine_id, type, started_at, ended_at, duration_min, work_order_id, cause)
Export the singleton: export const preventiveMaintenanceEngine = new PreventiveMaintenanceEngine()

Add dispatcher actions to businessDispatcher.ts z.enum: 'pm_schedule_create', 'pm_schedule_list', 'pm_work_order_generate', 'pm_complete', 'pm_overdue_alerts'. Add case handlers: pm_schedule_create calls preventiveMaintenanceEngine.createSchedule(args), pm_schedule_list calls listSchedules(args), pm_work_order_generate calls generateWorkOrder(args.schedule_id, args.scheduled_date), pm_complete calls completeWorkOrder(args.work_order_id, args), pm_overdue_alerts calls getOverdueAlerts()

Add schemas in src/schemas/businessActionSchemas.ts for all 5 new actions. pm_schedule_create: machine_id (string required), machine_name (string required), task_name (string required), trigger_type (z.enum(['calendar','hours']) required), interval_days (number optional), interval_hours (number optional), parts_list (array of PMPart objects optional), estimated_duration_min (number required), instructions (string required). pm_schedule_list: machine_id (string optional), overdue_only (boolean optional). pm_work_order_generate: schedule_id (string required), scheduled_date (string required). pm_complete: work_order_id (string required), labor_hours (number required), notes (string optional), parts_used (array optional). pm_overdue_alerts: no required fields. No .passthrough() on any schema

Create web/src/pages/PreventiveMaintenancePage.tsx. Use React 19 hooks. On mount, call GET /api/erp/pm-schedules and GET /api/erp/pm-overdue-alerts. Render: (a) top row of 3 stat cards — Total Schedules, Overdue (red badge if >0), Due This Week; (b) calendar view showing upcoming PM dates for the next 30 days (use a simple div-based grid for Mon-Sun columns, mark days with PM tasks); (c) overdue alerts table with columns Machine, Task, Days Overdue, Action (Generate Work Order button); (d) full schedules table with columns Machine, Task, Trigger, Next Due, Last Completed, Action (View Work Orders). All data calls go through web/src/api/client.ts functions

Add client functions to web/src/api/client.ts: pmScheduleCreate(params), pmScheduleList(filters?), pmWorkOrderGenerate(scheduleId, scheduledDate), pmComplete(workOrderId, params), pmOverdueAlerts(). Each calls the corresponding businessDispatcher action via the existing POST /api/mcp or equivalent RPC path
Add the route to web/src/App.tsx (or router file): path='/app/maintenance' element=<PreventiveMaintenancePage /> behind clearance_level >= 'lead' guard
Run npm run build:fast and fix all TypeScript errors before marking complete

units.title: Create EquipmentAssetEngine + EquipmentAssetPage

steps.instruction: Read src/engines/PreventiveMaintenanceEngine.ts (just created) to ensure EquipmentAssetEngine follows the same file structure and PersistenceBridge patterns

Create src/engines/EquipmentAssetEngine.ts. Define interfaces: AssetRecord { id, asset_tag, name, category: 'machine' | 'fixture' | 'gage' | 'tooling' | 'other', manufacturer, model_number, serial_number, location, purchase_date: string, purchase_cost: number, salvage_value: number, useful_life_years: number, depreciation_method: 'straight_line' | 'macrs_5yr' | 'macrs_7yr', current_book_value: number, status: 'active' | 'disposed' | 'transferred', calibration_required: boolean, last_calibration_date: string | undefined, next_calibration_date: string | undefined, calibration_interval_days: number | undefined, notes: string | undefined, created_at: string }, AssetTransfer { id, asset_id, from_location, to_location, transferred_at: string, transferred_by: string, reason: string }, DepreciationSchedule { asset_id, year: number, beginning_book_value: number, depreciation_amount: number, ending_book_value: number, cumulative_depreciation: number }
Implement EquipmentAssetEngine class with private Maps: assets: Map<string, AssetRecord>, assetTransfers: Map<string, AssetTransfer>. In constructor, call persistenceBridge.register() for both Maps

Implement registerAsset(params: Omit<AssetRecord, 'id' | 'current_book_value' | 'created_at'>): AssetRecord — assigns id, sets current_book_value = purchase_cost - computeDepreciation(purchase_cost, salvage_value, useful_life_years, depreciation_method, monthsSincePurchase), stores in assets Map, calls persist()

Implement computeDepreciation(purchaseCost: number, salvageValue: number, usefulLifeYears: number, method: string, monthsElapsed: number): number — for 'straight_line': annual = (purchaseCost - salvageValue) / usefulLifeYears; return Math.min(annual * (monthsElapsed / 12), purchaseCost - salvageValue). For 'macrs_5yr': use IRS MACRS 5-year half-year convention rates [20, 32, 19.2, 11.52, 11.52, 5.76] percent array applied by year index (floor(monthsElapsed/12)). For 'macrs_7yr': rates [14.29, 24.49, 17.49, 12.49, 8.93, 8.92, 8.93, 4.46] percent. Return cumulative depreciation through the elapsed period. Never exceed purchaseCost - salvageValue

Implement getDepreciationSchedule(assetId: string): DepreciationSchedule[] — computes year-by-year schedule from purchase_date through end of useful_life_years, returning one row per year with beginning_book_value, depreciation_amount, ending_book_value, cumulative_depreciation
Implement listAssets(filters?: { category?: string; location?: string; calibration_required?: boolean; status?: string }): AssetRecord[] — returns filtered list. Sort by name ascending

Implement transferAsset(assetId: string, params: { to_location: string; transferred_by: string; reason: string }): AssetTransfer — updates asset.location, creates AssetTransfer record, stores in assetTransfers, calls persist() on both Maps

Implement getDueCalibrations(daysAhead?: number): Array<{ asset: AssetRecord; days_until_due: number }> — for assets with calibration_required = true, compute days until next_calibration_date. Return those where days_until_due <= (daysAhead ?? 30). Sort by days_until_due ascending

Add ENTITY_CONFIGS in BusinessStore.ts for assets (knownColumns: id, asset_tag, name, category, manufacturer, model_number, serial_number, location, purchase_date, purchase_cost, salvage_value, useful_life_years, depreciation_method, current_book_value, status, calibration_required, last_calibration_date, next_calibration_date, calibration_interval_days, notes, created_at) and asset_transfers (knownColumns: id, asset_id, from_location, to_location, transferred_at, transferred_by, reason)
Export singleton: export const equipmentAssetEngine = new EquipmentAssetEngine()
Add to businessDispatcher.ts z.enum: 'asset_register', 'asset_list', 'asset_depreciation', 'asset_transfer', 'asset_due_calibrations'. Add case handlers calling the corresponding engine methods

Add schemas in businessActionSchemas.ts: asset_register with all AssetRecord fields except id/current_book_value/created_at; asset_list with optional filters; asset_depreciation with asset_id (string required); asset_transfer with asset_id, to_location, transferred_by, reason (all string required); asset_due_calibrations with days_ahead (number optional). No .passthrough()

Create web/src/pages/EquipmentAssetPage.tsx. Render: (a) summary stats row: Total Assets count, Total Book Value (sum of current_book_value), Calibrations Due This Month (count from getDueCalibrations(30)); (b) filter bar with dropdowns for category, location, status; (c) asset table with columns Asset Tag, Name, Category, Location, Purchase Cost, Book Value, Status, Cal Due, Actions (View Depreciation Schedule, Transfer); (d) Depreciation Schedule modal: shows year-by-year table for the selected asset; (e) Transfer modal: to_location text input + reason text input + submit. Wire all actions to client functions
Add client functions: assetRegister(params), assetList(filters?), assetDepreciation(assetId), assetTransfer(assetId, params), assetDueCalibrations(daysAhead?) in web/src/api/client.ts
Add route /app/assets -> EquipmentAssetPage in App.tsx behind clearance_level >= 'lead' guard
Run npm run build:fast and fix all TypeScript errors

units.title: Wire CalibrationEngine to CalibrationPage

steps.instruction: Read src/engines/CalibrationEngine.ts in full (334 lines) to catalogue all public methods, their signatures, return types, and Map names. List every method before writing any frontend code

Check src/tools/dispatchers/businessDispatcher.ts for existing CalibrationEngine actions. Identify which of calSchedule_create, calRecord, calCertificate_upload, calOverdue_alerts are already wired vs which are missing

For any missing actions, add to businessDispatcher.ts z.enum and add case handlers. Required actions: cal_schedule_create (creates a calibration schedule), cal_record (records a completed calibration with result: 'pass' | 'fail' | 'conditional'), cal_overdue_alerts (returns gages/assets past due), cal_lockout (sets a gage status to 'do_not_use' with reason), cal_unlock (re-enables a locked-out gage after recalibration). Wire to CalibrationEngine methods

For any missing schemas, add to businessActionSchemas.ts: cal_schedule_create (gage_id string required, gage_name string required, interval_days number required, responsible_tech string required), cal_record (gage_id string required, performed_by string required, result z.enum(['pass','fail','conditional']) required, certificate_ref string optional, notes string optional), cal_overdue_alerts (no required fields), cal_lockout (gage_id string required, reason string required), cal_unlock (gage_id string required). No .passthrough()

Create web/src/pages/CalibrationPage.tsx. On mount: call calOverdueAlerts() and calScheduleList() (add cal_schedule_list action if missing). Render: (a) summary stat cards — Total Gages, Overdue (red if >0), Due This Month, Locked Out (orange badge if >0); (b) overdue alerts banner (collapsible yellow bar) listing gage name + days overdue for each overdue gage; (c) locked-out gages section (red border cards) showing gage name, lockout reason, Unlock button (calls calUnlock() — requires confirmation modal); (d) full calibration schedule table with columns Gage, Interval (days), Last Cal, Next Due, Last Result (green PASS / red FAIL / orange CONDITIONAL badge), Assigned Tech, Actions (Record Cal, Lock Out)

Add Record Calibration modal in CalibrationPage.tsx: fields — Performed By (text input), Result (select: pass/fail/conditional), Certificate Ref (text input, optional), Notes (textarea). On submit, call calRecord(). If result = 'fail', automatically prompt: 'Do you want to lock out this gage?' with a reason textarea. If yes, also call calLockout()

Add a Gage R&R tracking section: a table below the main schedules table labeled 'Gage R&R History' with columns Gage, Study Date, Operator Count, %GR&R, Status (<=10% = Acceptable green, 10-30% = Marginal yellow, >30% = Unacceptable red). Add dispatcher action cal_grr_record (gage_id, study_date, operator_count, percent_grr all required) and client function calGrrRecord(params). Wire Add R&R Study button to open a simple modal

phases.title: Compliance & Audit Management
phases.description: Add OSHA incident/near-miss tracking with OSHA 300/300A/301 log generation. Add ISO/AS9100 internal audit scheduling with finding and CAPA tracking. Enhance QualityManagementEngine with full 8D workflow. All pages behind appropriate clearance levels.

units.title: Add OSHA Compliance Page

steps.instruction: Read src/engines/HRComplianceEngine.ts in full to understand the training record interface and hr_training_* dispatcher actions already available. Note exact method signatures for hr_training_list and hr_training_record
Check businessDispatcher.ts for existing osha_* actions. If none exist, plan to add all 4

Define new interfaces in a new file src/engines/OSHAComplianceEngine.ts: OSHAIncident { id, incident_date: string, employee_id: string | undefined, employee_name: string | undefined, location: string, description: string, injury_type: 'injury' | 'illness' | 'near_miss' | 'property_damage', body_part_affected: string | undefined, days_away: number, days_restricted: number, medical_treatment: 'first_aid' | 'medical_beyond_first_aid' | 'hospitalization' | 'fatality', recordable: boolean, osha_case_number: string | undefined, reported_by: string, anonymous: boolean, witnesses: string[], corrective_actions: string[], created_at: string }, PPEAssignment { id, employee_id: string, ppe_type: string, size: string | undefined, issued_date: string, issued_by: string, condition: 'good' | 'worn' | 'replace' }
Implement OSHAComplianceEngine with private Maps: incidents: Map<string, OSHAIncident>, ppeAssignments: Map<string, PPEAssignment>. Register both with PersistenceBridge in constructor

Implement createIncident(params: Omit<OSHAIncident, 'id' | 'created_at'>): OSHAIncident — auto-determines recordable = true if medical_treatment != 'first_aid' || days_away > 0 || days_restricted > 0. For anonymous incidents, store employee_id = 'ANONYMOUS' and do not store employee_name. Calls persist()

Implement generateOSHA300Log(year: number): OSHA300Row[] — filters incidents where recordable = true and year(incident_date) == year. Maps each to OSHA300Row { case_number, employee_name: anonymous ? 'Privacy Case' : employee_name, job_title, date_of_injury, where_event_occurred, describe_injury, days_away, days_restricted, injury_type_checkboxes }. Returns array sorted by incident_date

Implement generateOSHA300ASummary(year: number): OSHA300ASummary — aggregates OSHA300Log for the year into totals: total_injuries, total_illnesses, total_days_away, total_days_restricted, total_deaths. Returns the summary object with establishment name 'PRISM Manufacturing' as placeholder
Implement assignPPE(params: Omit<PPEAssignment, 'id'>): PPEAssignment — stores in ppeAssignments, calls persist()
Implement listPPEByEmployee(employeeId: string): PPEAssignment[] — returns all PPE assignments for the employee. Adds a flag needs_replacement = (condition === 'replace')

Add ENTITY_CONFIGS in BusinessStore.ts for osha_incidents (knownColumns: id, incident_date, employee_id, employee_name, location, injury_type, body_part_affected, days_away, days_restricted, medical_treatment, recordable, osha_case_number, reported_by, anonymous, created_at; jsonColumns: witnesses, corrective_actions) and ppe_assignments (knownColumns: id, employee_id, ppe_type, size, issued_date, issued_by, condition)
Export singleton: export const oshaComplianceEngine = new OSHAComplianceEngine()

Add to businessDispatcher.ts z.enum: 'osha_incident_create', 'osha_log_300', 'osha_near_miss', 'osha_ppe_assign'. Case handlers: osha_incident_create -> createIncident(args), osha_log_300 -> generateOSHA300Log(args.year), osha_near_miss -> createIncident({...args, injury_type: 'near_miss', recordable: false}), osha_ppe_assign -> assignPPE(args)

Add schemas in businessActionSchemas.ts: osha_incident_create (incident_date required, location required, injury_type z.enum required, medical_treatment z.enum required, days_away number default 0, days_restricted number default 0, employee_id optional string, anonymous boolean default false, description string required, reported_by string required), osha_log_300 (year number required), osha_near_miss (same as osha_incident_create minus recordable), osha_ppe_assign (employee_id, ppe_type, issued_date, issued_by all required string; size optional; condition z.enum default 'good'). Returns { connected: true, version, shop_name } on 200, throws with error message on failure. Stores config in a private e2Config Map, calls persist(). (b) e2SyncStatus(): { last_sync: string | undefined; jobs_synced: number; employees_synced: number; invoices_synced: number; errors: string[] } — returns current sync state from a private e2SyncState Map

Implement e2SyncNow(): Promise<E2SyncResult> — define E2SyncResult interface { synced_at: string; jobs_pulled: number; employees_pulled: number; time_entries_pushed: number; invoices_pushed: number; conflicts: E2Conflict[]; errors: string[] }, E2Conflict { entity_type: string; entity_id: string; prism_value: unknown; e2_value: unknown; resolution: 'e2_wins' | 'prism_wins' }. Sync logic: (1) GET {base_url}/api/v1/jobs — pull jobs from E2, upsert into PRISM JobLifecycleEngine (E2 is source of truth for job/customer data). (2) GET {base_url}/api/v1/employees — pull employees, upsert into PRISM EmployeeEngine. (3) GET PRISM time entries since last_sync, POST to {base_url}/api/v1/time-entries (PRISM is source of truth for time). (4) GET PRISM completed jobs not yet invoiced, POST to {base_url}/api/v1/invoices. Apply conflict resolution rules: E2 wins on customer/job data fields, PRISM wins on hours/cost fields. Store result in e2SyncState, call persist(). Handle all HTTP errors with try/catch and record in errors array

Add qboSyncInvoices(): Promise<QBOInvoiceSyncResult> to IntegrationAdapterEngine.ts — define QBOInvoiceSyncResult { synced_at: string; invoices_created: number; invoices_updated: number; errors: string[] }. Logic: (1) Get all PRISM invoices with status = 'approved' and qbo_invoice_id = undefined. (2) For each, POST to QBO API endpoint /v3/company/{realmId}/invoice with QBO invoice payload mapping (customer_ref from job customer_name, line items from invoice lines, due date, total amount). (3) On 200, store returned QBO invoice ID back on the PRISM invoice record (add qbo_invoice_id field to invoice interface if not present). Handle 401 by triggering OAuth refresh. All errors caught and added to errors array. Calls persist() after updates

Add qboSyncPayments(): Promise<QBOPaymentSyncResult> — define QBOPaymentSyncResult { synced_at: string; payments_synced: number; invoices_marked_paid: number; errors: string[] }. Logic: (1) GET QBO /v3/company/{realmId}/query?query=SELECT * FROM Payment WHERE TxnDate >= :last_sync. (2) For each payment, match PRISM invoice by qbo_invoice_id. (3) Mark matched PRISM invoices as 'paid' with payment_date and payment_amount. Calls persist()

Add qboReconcile(): Promise<QBOReconcileResult> — define QBOReconcileResult { period: string; prism_gl_total: number; qbo_gl_total: number; discrepancies: QBODiscrepancy[]; matched: number }. Logic: GET QBO Trial Balance report for current month. Compare total revenue/COGS/liability totals against PRISM GL totals from ActualCostEngine. Build discrepancies list for any line items differing by more than $0.01. Return the reconcile result (do not auto-correct — report only)
